title: GAP: Guided Diffusion for A Priori Transition State Sampling
experiments_summary: The ASTRA workflow was evaluated across five systems using a common pipeline: a score-based diffusion model with Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is trained on MD data of metastable states, Score-Based Interpolation (SBI) guides the reverse diffusion to the equal-density dividing surface, and Score-Aligned Ascent (SAA) refines samples using force-field-based saddle-point optimization with the reaction coordinate approximated from the score difference. Specific experimental setups are as follows: (1) 1D PES: a simple analytic double-well potential used as a minimal sanity check. (2) Müller-Brown Potential: a 2D analytic benchmark with three minima and two saddle points; 4,000 samples from the 'tiny' Raja et al. subset were used to train the diffusion model; states defined by y < 20 and y > 20. (3) Double-Path Potential: a synthetic 2D analytic potential with two distinct transition pathways; dataset generated via Langevin Dynamics, 4,000 samples used; states defined by x < 0 and x > 0. (4) Alanine Dipeptide: a 22-atom molecule; 2,500 configurations per state generated by 500 ps Langevin Dynamics at 300 K with 1 fs timestep; an EquiformerV2-based diffusion model trained with AdamW optimizer, cosine DDPM schedule over 1,000 timesteps for 500 epochs; SAA run for 1,000 steps with Adam optimizer; committor values computed from 100 replicas of 1 ps Langevin Dynamics simulations per sample configuration. (5) Chignolin: a coarse-grained 10-residue protein using the DESRES dataset; conformations with committor values between 0.0001 and 0.9999 removed from training; a pre-trained model from Arts et al. was fine-tuned with a group embedding for conditional generation; SAA run for 100 steps; committor values computed using a pre-trained ML committor predictor from Kang et al. Ablation studies on the 2D potentials isolated contributions of SBI (isodensity vs. simple score averaging) and SAA. Baseline comparisons used linear interpolation (after Kabsch alignment) and geodesic interpolation based on radius of gyration, evaluated on alanine dipeptide. Validation of the reaction coordinate approximation was performed by computing cosine similarity between the score-difference vector and the true reaction coordinate on the Müller-Brown and Double-Path potentials. Structural validation of chignolin TS ensembles was performed by visual comparison of ASTRA-generated structures against reference configurations from Kang et al., and by projecting samples onto TICA coordinates.
